submissions.findingTextShort: Acute oral sodium propionate increased resting energy expenditure and lipid oxidation without changing glucose or insulin.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: In a randomized crossover study of 18 healthy adults, oral sodium propionate tablets totaling 6845 mg over 180 minutes increased resting energy expenditure and whole-body lipid oxidation acutely, while glucose and insulin concentrations did not change; this is short-term substrate physiology rather than evidence of durable weight loss or metabolic disease benefit.
submissions.usageContext: Acute oral sodium propionate tablets over 180 minutes
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Acute surrogate endpoints cannot establish chronic weight-management or cardiometabolic efficacy.

submissions.findingTextShort: Calcium propionate activated counter-regulatory hormones and endogenous glucose production in a randomized human crossover study.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: In a randomized placebo-controlled crossover study of 28 healthy adults after a propionate-free diet, 1500 mg calcium propionate increased glucagon and norepinephrine at rest and increased counter-regulatory hormones and endogenous glucose production under clamp conditions, leading the authors to describe exogenous propionate as a potential metabolic disruptor.
submissions.usageContext: Oral calcium propionate 1500 mg in a food-preservative exposure model
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Specific calcium-propionate exposure and acute physiology; should constrain generic benefit claims without being generalized to endogenous microbiota-derived propionate.

submissions.findingTextShort: A 12-month IPE trial did not prevent weight gain compared with inulin.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: In the multicenter double-blind iPREVENT trial, 270 adults at risk of weight gain were randomized to 10 g per day inulin-propionate ester or 10 g per day inulin for 12 months; IPE did not prevent weight gain versus inulin and most body-composition and fasting biomarker outcomes did not differ.
submissions.populationContext: Two hundred seventy adults aged 20 to 40 years at risk of weight gain
submissions.usageContext: Colon-targeted inulin-propionate ester 10 g per day versus inulin for 12 months
submissions.uncertaintyNote: IPE is an engineered delivery conjugate and active-control comparison, not generic oral propionate; null long-duration outcome should cap attractive acute mechanism narratives.

submissions.findingTextShort: Propionate evidence requires separate owners for endogenous propionate, salts, preservative exposure, IPE, and rectal or mixed-SCFA delivery.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: Human propionate research uses chemically and clinically distinct propositions including endogenous microbiota-derived propionate, sodium propionate, calcium propionate food-preservative exposure, colon-targeted inulin-propionate ester, and rectal or mixed-SCFA delivery; shared released propionate does not make these interventions interchangeable for efficacy, dose, safety, or recommendation.
submissions.populationContext: Human propionate literature across healthy, overweight, and metabolic contexts
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Relationship/governance finding; does not assign one risk or benefit profile to every propionate exposure.
